statement: GMI Cloud's GPU-backed loan drew commitments of about NT$30 billion ($947 million) against the NT$13.9 billion it sought, showing lenders will finance AI compute on the security of chip-derived cash flows.
why: Oversubscribed collateralized lending loosens the financing constraint on the marginal GPU buyer, letting neoclouds order more capacity than equity alone would allow.

impact.mechanism: Bank appetite for loans backed by the sale of computing power lowers the cost of capital for GPU buildouts, converting into additional accelerator orders.

evidence.excerpt: GMI Cloud, an Nvidia partner, secured commitments for more than double the amount it was seeking in a loan backed by the sale of computing power from advanced chips.
